summary: Medicine Bow forest tower completed 1912 on Barrett Ridge; in use through 1930, duties moved to Slash Ridge around 1949; listed as gone.

facts.status_note: listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association and firelookout.com; no removal year, description or remains in the sources

staffing.status: fire lookout station maintained on the ridge in 1918; district rangers worked it as a secondary lookout in hazardous periods in 1921

events.note: tower completed under the forest supervisor's direction; made four forest towers in view of all parts of the forest, each linked by telephone
July 1918: fire lookout station maintained on the ridge; Forest Service telephone line reached a high point there, and a family camping on Barrett Creek called several local people over it
district rangers served as lookouts at Barrett Ridge as a secondary site during especially hazardous fire periods
towers now in place on Barrett Ridge, at Long Lake and on Bridger Peak; named as sites where temporary observers could be posted in hazardous conditions
lookout duties transferred to Slash Ridge (c.1949)

evidence.quote: During his absence he supervised the construction of a lookout tower on Barrett Ridge, in the western portion of the forest.

evidence.supports: completion made four towers within the forest from which all parts can be watched
evidence.quote: The completion of the tower makes four within the forest which all parts can be watched for possible fires.

evidence.supports: towers connected to the supervisor's office and ranger headquarters by telephone
evidence.quote: Each is connected with the supervisor's office and the ranger headquarters by telephone

evidence.supports: July 1918: a family camping on Barrett Creek called several local people from the ridge summit
evidence.quote: has been camping for several days on Barrett Creek, in the Medicine Bow reserve, called up several local people Tuesday morning from the summit of Barrett Ridge

evidence.supports: 1918 fire lookout station maintained on the ridge, reached by Forest Service telephone line
evidence.quote: talking over the Forest Service line which terminates at a high point on the ridge where a fire lookout station is maintained

evidence.supports: 1921: district rangers served as lookouts on secondary sites in especially hazardous fire periods; Barrett Ridge among them
evidence.quote: the district forest rangers serve as lookouts on additional secondary lookouts on Jay's Roost, near Keystone, Barrett Ridge at the head of Cottonwood creek

evidence.supports: lookout duties transferred to Slash Ridge around 1949
evidence.quote: c.1949: Lookout duties were transferred to Slash Ridge.

evidence.supports: 1930 item: other towers now in place on Barrett Ridge, at Long Lake and on Bridger Peak, as observer sites in hazardous conditions (the quoted 'This tower' is the new Jays Roost tower)
evidence.quote: This tower, together with others now in place on Barrett ridge, at Long lake and on Bridger peak, will permit of temporary observers being placed at these points in the event of hazardous conditions.

evidence.supports: listed as a tower that is gone
about 15 miles northeast of Riverside, Carbon County

sources.title: Fire Lookouts Extravaganza in the Rocky Mountains

notes_for_editor: The brief's record also carries a second coordinate pair (41.30083, -106.49806, labelled west_us_lookouts); the FFLA inventory gives 41.32657, -106.52627, which is used here. The second pair's source was not checked. The 1918 and 1921 entries come from the Saratoga Sun and Laramie Republican reprints on the weebly page, and the 1930 entry from the Casper Tribune-Herald item quoted on the Adventr blog. No removal year, description or current-site detail was found.
